docs.gestures.component: ONE PAGE PER GESTURE, and each of them shows that gesture and nothing else.
A gesture is a seam worth looking at alone. A card carries a dozen capabilities and a menu on
top, and when a hold does not fire on it there are ten places to look. Here there is one gesture
per page, so "it did not move" has exactly one meaning.
A PRESS AND A CARRY WANT DIFFERENT DESKS. `Hold` and `Tap` are about the press itself, which has
nothing to do with what is under it — so they are one plain square, a target rather than a
picture. A grab does not work like that: the finger picks a thing up and takes it somewhere, so
those pages stand on a map with pieces on it and a camera over it.
docs.gestures.hold: HOLD THE SQUARE. Half a second of a finger that does not travel, and the tile shivers.
The shiver is the answer to a gesture that has just changed meaning. Without it a player who
gets no reply lifts their finger to check — cancelling the very gesture they were making.
docs.gestures.tap: TAP THE SQUARE, and tap beside it.
A tap is the other half of the same press, and the pair is what makes either legible: one
finger, one square, and the meaning turns on whether it leaves quickly or stays.
docs.gestures.grab: PICK A PIECE UP AND PUT IT DOWN SOMEWHERE ELSE. Two cards, a die and a knight, on a map that
does not fit the glass: a finger on a piece moves the piece, a finger on bare map moves the view,
and the two never argue about a hand.
The carry here is BARE — the piece is exactly where the finger is, at the size it has always
been, at the angle it was lying at. Nothing eases, nothing banks, nothing pops. That is the
honest floor of the gesture, and the switch on the panel is what puts the kit's own feel back on
One thing is not part of the switch: the POSITION. A held thing rides the hand 1:1 on either
setting, because a lag there reads as a dropped frame rather than as weight.
docs.gestures.grabPhysics: THE SAME MAP, WITH THE CARRY'S PHYSICS ON from the first touch: the lift pops the piece up as the
hand closes on it, and the bank leans it into the direction it is being carried.
A page of its own rather than a different default on the one before it, because the pair is the
point. Everything the carry does beyond following the hand is a CHOICE the kit made, and a choice
cannot be told from a law until the two are open side by side.
docs.gestures.lift: HOW HIGH THE HAND HOLDS IT. The same map again, the same pieces, the same border and the same
finger ring — the one thing that changes is how far a piece comes UP when the hand closes on it.
On a desk seen from above, height IS this: a thing further from the glass covers more of it. The
engine has a rate for it (`RISE`), and the carry's own `lift` is that rate under a hand — the kit
asks for a polite six percent, and this page asks for a third of a card, which is the difference
between a piece that acknowledges the finger and one that is genuinely off the desk.
The height is this page's own number, so it survives the physics switch: turn the feel off and the
piece still rises, it just stops leaning on the way. That is the point of having it here — the
lean and the lift are two channels, and a page where one switch killed both could not say so.
docs.gestures.drop: LET GO, AND IT FALLS. The same map, the same pieces, the same border — what changes is the
release: the piece is not put down, it is dropped, from exactly the height the hand was holding
How it comes down is the piece's own business, and it is read off what the piece IS rather than
what it is called. A card takes its time and stays where it lands — it is the lightest thing here
and paper does not bounce. A die comes down hard and the desk throws it back, twice, before it
settles. A carved piece falls as fast as the die and lands like the lump of wood it is, with
AND THE LAST THING DROPPED IS ON TOP, because that is what a desk is. It is a place in the tree
and not a height: written as a height, every drop would raise the pile a little further off the
felt forever, and the piece would be hovering over a desk it is lying on.
